# When do extra reasoning, cross-language routing, and continual feedback change decisions?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/system-one/adaptive-decisions.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 4 topic entries / 4 representative comparisons

Adaptive decisions operate on three timelines. Selective Reasoning allocates reasoning and readout within one question; a cross-language cascade routes requests across backends; Jev-DLC uses observed feedback to change later requests. Capability evaluations establish a baseline without automatically validating any control strategy. Freeze or make choices before revealing the current test target.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Compute feedback and user feedback are different loops

Selective Reasoning observes intermediate distributions while the answer is unknown and decides whether to keep generating or read out. Jev-DLC receives accept/revoke after a request and changes the next request's state. The former cannot require the current gold answer to stop; the latter can use feedback without retroactively changing the score. They can be combined, but log per-question compute and generalization after cross-question adaptation separately.

Sources: [Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop](../../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en.md) · [Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback](../../../../system-one/2610.31521-jev-dlc/README-en.md)

### Well-calibrated probabilities are not the same as finding hard questions

Cross-language transfer uses ECE and Brier scores for calibration and measures error ranking with metrics such as risk–coverage. Selective Reasoning's normalized entropy measures concentration in the current distribution. A temperature can improve calibration without improving error ranking. Strong knowledge and weak math scores do not directly yield a per-question trigger. Set routing and budgets on validation, then measure tasks and languages independently.

Sources: [Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages](../../../../system-one/2610.14112-regional-transfer/README-en.md) · [Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop](../../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en.md) · [Specialized Decision Models vs. General-Purpose LLMs: Benchmarking Jev Across Knowledge, Reasoning, and Multilingual Tasks](../../../../system-one/2610.11978-jev-capability/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why do Selective Reasoning's intermediate readout and Jev-DLC's revoke update need different evaluation clocks? {#cross-within-versus-between-requests}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The intermediate read occurs before the current target is revealed and tests whether extra compute changes the current choice. A revoke has already revealed what should replace the old choice, so it can update only later requests. Rescoring the current response after feedback leaks the label into prediction and does not demonstrate continual adaptation.

    **Illustrative example:** For question 10, the model first selects A and then receives “change to B.” DLC can use that for question 11; question 10 is scored on A. Reading an intermediate distribution on question 10 happens before that feedback.

    Sources: [Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop](../../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en.md) · [Jev-DLC: Decision-Level Continual Learning from Typed Feedback](../../../../system-one/2610.31521-jev-dlc/README-en.md)

### Why test low-confidence routing and entropy stopping separately after calibration improves? {#cross-calibration-does-not-route-errors}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Calibration asks whether probabilities match aggregate correctness frequencies. Routing needs errors concentrated at low confidence, while entropy stopping sees only whether one distribution is concentrated. Cross-language transfer tests these separately. Selective Reasoning allocates budget with validation-selected controls; lower ECE alone does not show better early stopping or fallback.

    **Illustrative example:** Two models may each be correct 80% of the time in their 0.8-confidence bins. Across the full confidence ranking, one places more errors at the bottom while the other spreads errors across bins. That single bin cannot determine how much a cascade saves.

    Sources: [Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages](../../../../system-one/2610.14112-regional-transfer/README-en.md) · [Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop](../../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en.md)

### If a language or math task appears weak, can we try many routing fractions on test and report the best? {#cross-validation-budget-versus-test}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Capability measurements suggest checking coverage and errors by task but do not turn test into a strategy-selection set. Choose the smallest routing fraction that meets the validation macro-F1 target, then freeze it. Likewise, fix reasoning triggers and entropy thresholds in advance and preserve budget-forced cases.

    **Illustrative example:** Validation chooses to route the lowest-confidence 20% to the stronger model. Even if 30% looks better on test, it is not the predefined strategy unless evaluated on a separate confirmation set.

    Sources: [Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages](../../../../system-one/2610.14112-regional-transfer/README-en.md) · [Specialized Decision Models vs. General-Purpose LLMs: Benchmarking Jev Across Knowledge, Reasoning, and Multilingual Tasks](../../../../system-one/2610.11978-jev-capability/README-en.md) · [Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop](../../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en.md)
